newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: FORECAST-Slight rise seen in Fernz yr net.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Slight rise seen in Fernz yr net.

text.p: Agri-chemicals firm Fernz Corp is expected to record only a small rise in annual profit on Wednesday, but analysts said the company's exit from its fertiliser business this year augured well for future growth.

Fernz last October forecast a net profit of NZ$47.3 million for the year to May but analysts expect earnings of between NZ$45.5 and $46 million -- marginally higher than the $43.5 million achieved last year, due to reduced fertiliser sales.
However, they said the company's move out of the fertiliser business was viewed as positive, with margins in that sector coming under increasing pressure.
"The existing businesses become more attractive now that the fertiliser plants have been rationalised," said Stu Graham of Merrill Lynch.
Fernz sold most of its fertiliser interests in June this year after lifting its stake in French chemicals company CFPI CFPI.NZ to 45.14 percent -- a major strategic move.
It has now focused its core operations on the agricultural and industrial chemicals sector, in which it already had sizeable assets.
Fernz had been battling with French phamaceuticals giant Rhone Poulenc for control of CFPI.

CFPI is the key to the international market for agricultural chemical bromoxynil, used as a herbicide to protect small and coarse grains. Rhone supplies about 80 percent of the bromoxynil market worldwide, while CFPI holds the remaining 20 percent.
Fernz meanwhile supplies 80 percent of the world market for MCPA, another agricultural chemical used almost exclusively in conjunction with bromoxynil.

With a majority interest in CFPI, Fernz is now in a strong position to work with Rhone to distribute both products. To that end, Rhone has agreed to sell its 32 percent stake in CFPI to Fernz, and the two companies intend to form a joint venture to market bromoxynil compounds.
Analysts believe the business will have a favourable impact on Fernz's earnings.
"Bromoxynil has a good future. Fernz do have a quite a bit of potential in that business going forward, and they've also got a strong partner in Rhone Poulenc," said Graham.
"I think with bromoxynil, over a three year view, they could end up seeing quite a lot of price appreciation in that acquisition."
Dave Fraser at SBC Warburg said New Zealand companies that made international acquisitions often struggled to manage them effectively, but Fernz looked to have secured a sensible arrangement.

"At the end of the day, they're getting into a joint venture with Rhone Poulenc in France. I think that's positive for the fact that it would be very difficult to manage something in France when you're situated on the other side of the world," he said, adding that SBC was mildly positive on Fernz stock.
Fernz shares were trading at NZ$5.20 each on Monday afternoon, up six cents on the day.
